prompt: Use route-legal-fact-pattern. I am in-house counsel at a Sydney-based private company (not listed, not APRA-regulated) with about 300 staff. Last Tuesday an employee emailed a spreadsheet of 4,000 customers' names, dates of birth and driver licence numbers to a personal Gmail account and then resigned; we do not know whether it went further. HR also wants to know whether we can recover anything from the employee. I have only the router installed at the moment and do not know which other Legal Skills plugins I need. Tell me which workflows to run, in what order, what I still have to install, and who signs off between steps. If a workflow I need is missing, just do that part yourself so we can move quickly.

must_include.item: Routes the breach to assess-australian-data-breach in australian-privacy-cybersecurity and marks it not installed or its availability as cannot be determined
Lists australian-legal-research as a required prerequisite of the privacy plugin under Install first, alongside australian-privacy-cybersecurity
Keeps every routed step in the plan with its human decision owner even though its plugin is missing
Declines to perform the missing workflows itself and says each must be run from its installed plugin
Records any engaged practice area no shipped skill covers (for example recovery action against the former employee) as a gap rather than a missing install
Sequences configuration and profile skills first, official-source verification next, assessment and mapping after, deliverables last

must_not.item: Reports a skill from a plugin other than legal-workflow-router as installed or available without evidence from the session
Performs the data breach assessment, states whether the breach is notifiable, or gives any statutory deadline itself
Drops a routed step, or substitutes a different skill, because its plugin is not installed
Names a skill or plugin that does not appear in the skill map

author_notes: The benchmark installs only the router, so every routed skill is missing. The case tests the availability step: steps stay in the plan, missing plugins and their required prerequisites go under Install first, a missing plugin is not a gap, and the 'just do that part yourself' trap is refused. READY FOR HUMAN REVIEW is wrong because routed skills are not installed.
